items.title: Is Intel Stock a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?
items.summary: Intel reported strong Q2 2026 earnings with adjusted EPS of $0.42 (double expectations) and revenue of $16.1 billion (nearly $1.7B above estimates), driven by surging AI demand. However, the stock fell 33% in the past month due to concerns over raised capex guidance ($20B for 2026, with 2027 expected to be significantly higher) and potential shareholder dilution. While the company benefits from AI infrastructure buildout, the stock trades at 59x forward earnings and carries high volatility risk dependent on sustained AI demand.

items.title: Intel Just Posted Its Fastest Revenue Growth in More Than 15 Years, but the Stock Is Falling. Here's What's Going On.
items.summary: Intel reported strong Q2 2026 results with 25% year-over-year revenue growth to $16.1 billion and a swing to $0.42 adjusted EPS profitability, driven by AI and data center demand. Despite initial 12% after-hours gains, the stock fell below Thursday's closing price by Friday as investors reassessed the company's 60x P/E valuation, which assumes sustained high growth rates.

items.title: Where Will Intel Stock Be in 5 Years?
items.summary: Intel stock has surged 425% over the past year under new CEO Lip-Bu Tan's leadership, driven by breakthroughs in chip manufacturing technology like the 18A process. However, the gains appear largely speculative as Intel's actual revenue growth remains modest at 7% year-over-year, with continued net losses. While Tan's track record suggests potential for a turnaround and the AI chip market projects strong growth, Intel still lags competitors significantly in revenue expansion, making it a speculative investment for risk-tolerant investors.

items.title: This AI Chip Stock Just Signed Massive Deals With 3 Hyperscalers, and It Still Looks Like a Great Buy Right Now (Hint: Not Nvidia or Intel)
items.summary: Qualcomm has signed major deals with three hyperscalers and expects its data center chip business to grow from nearly zero to $15 billion by 2029. The company projects $5 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2027 and expects EPS to climb to over $18 by 2029, representing 18% annualized growth. Trading at less than 18 times forward earnings, the stock appears undervalued relative to its growth prospects.

items.title: Micron vs. Intel: Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Both Micron and Intel have surged over 200% year-to-date on AI tailwinds. Intel is positioned for future growth through its AI chips, CPUs, and foundry services, with government support. However, Micron emerges as the better buy due to its explosive current growth—quadrupling revenue year-over-year with a 7.4 forward P/E ratio, compared to Intel's 147 P/E and 7% revenue growth.

items.title: Intel vs. Navitas: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Intel and Navitas Semiconductor represent different semiconductor strategies: Intel is pivoting to a foundry model for chip manufacturing while Navitas specializes in next-generation power materials like gallium nitride for AI and EVs. Intel shows stronger near-term momentum with revenue growth acceleration, while Navitas faces recovery risks after exiting its Chinese consumer business to focus on AI markets.

items.title: How Intel Is Packaging the Future of American Chips
items.summary: Intel has surged 281.8% year-to-date by pivoting to become a sovereign foundry powerhouse, with a new advanced packaging division led by SK hynix veteran Seok-Hee Lee. The company secured preliminary agreements with Apple for M-series chip production and a $5 billion strategic investment from NVIDIA. However, Intel trades at a stretched 223x forward P/E ratio with massive operating deficits, requiring flawless execution and near-term margin compression to justify current valuations.

items.title: AMD vs. Intel: Which Stock Is the Better Buy Right Now?
items.summary: Both AMD and Intel have surged amid AI chip demand, with Intel up 258% in 2026 backed by $9B in federal government support and a new Apple partnership. However, Intel's valuation is extremely expensive with P/E ratios of 161 and 904, while AMD offers stronger fundamentals with 38% revenue growth and a more reasonable valuation. AMD appears the safer choice, though Intel could outperform if government support continues.

items.title: Is Intel the Comeback Stock of the Decade?
items.summary: Intel has experienced a remarkable sevenfold stock price increase over 14 months, rising from $18.84 to around $130 per share, driven by CEO Lip-Bu Tan's execution of the foundry strategy, the 18A process node success, CHIPS Act funding, and growing data center CPU demand. While other stocks like Carvana have achieved higher percentage returns, Intel's comeback is arguably more significant from a macro perspective as it strengthens U.S. semiconductor competitiveness and reduces dependence on Taiwan.
